pr_title: mgmt: mcumgr: Fix Bluetooth transport issues
pr_body:
This fixes issues with the Bluetooth SMP transport whereby deadlocks could arise from connection references being held in long-lasting mcumgr command processing functions.

Fixes #51653
Fixes #51714
pr_comments:
@de-nordic https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/51757#discussion_r1014223549

Yeah, I will bring this up with the other bluetooth maintainers, as I've seen a bunch of cases where we want to do exactly that, check that the conn object is still pointing to the connection (session?) we thought it was.
Maybe having the cpu ticks or uptime would be enough, yeah. It would also double-up as a session-length counter (until it wraps, that is). 
I'll see what I can do to have something like that as an official API sometime in the near future.

> @de-nordic [#51757 (comment)](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/51757#discussion_r1014223549)
> 
> Yeah, I will bring this up with the other bluetooth maintainers, as I've seen a bunch of cases where we want to do exactly that, check that the conn object is still pointing to the connection (session?) we thought it was. Maybe having the cpu ticks or uptime would be enough, yeah. It would also double-up as a session-length counter (until it wraps, that is). I'll see what I can do to have something like that as an official API sometime in the near future.

Having some unique identifier passed from BLE susbystem would be nice, because that would free us, and other subsystems, from figuring out to add additional layer of identification.
Hashes on objects does not make sense, due to statistical reasons, and random values would require recording values in use.  Value like ticks or time since system startup or first connection are increasing automatically (are monotonic, as much as type size allows before they overlap) giving unique identifier each time when picked as long as precision allows to obtain different values for closest possible connections, and as long as they have range that is able to hold value longer than time the connection information is held by a system.

> Please release notes entry for MCUmgr describing addition, and to fixed bugs section.

Release notes are already present, this fully fixes the previous attempt at the fix

Question: why aren't we allocating the id in `smp_bt_chr_write` after this:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/4bae4f426ff4c5e4b84f29d8150789db1c7c569b/subsys/mgmt/mcumgr/transport/smp_bt.c#L262-L264
and before
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/4bae4f426ff4c5e4b84f29d8150789db1c7c569b/subsys/mgmt/mcumgr/transport/smp_bt.c#L233

In case when reassembly is enabled this basically can be done by having static counter within function that will be incremented every time function is invoked.

Non re-assembly case is a little bit trickier because there may be multiple buffers per request, but this can probably be resolved my doing conn to id map.

> Question: why aren't we allocating the id in smp_bt_chr_write after this:

The way it works here is much simpler and works for all queued packets, i.e. a device can queue up 5 commands and disconnect, it does not need different IDs for each command, they should be the same.

Reverted back to an incrementing counter as I don't see the value in tick count, it adds nothing useful and still needs the same != 0 check. Have allowed cpd to be null instead of asserting in the get function and added null checks and LOG_ERR() output on it being null, moved ID generation to alloc function.

@nordicjm - in order to backport this change, the `backport v2.7-branch` label should be added to this PR. That would kick off the automated backport. Is there a reason that wasn't done? I should mention, that even if an automated backport fails, you can still modify it (it gets a special backport branch).

@cfriedt I didn't do it from this because the code in 2.7 is so vastly outdated compared to main (e.g. different filenames and paths, different functions, different code) that none of it applies and it was just easier to manually copy and paste the bits into the 2.7 tree

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Application with buffer that cannot unref it in disconnect handler leads to advertising issues
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
This issue has been found with a peripheral zephyr device which supports 1 connection, the application works by receiving BT data and then putting it into a fifo to be processed by a dedicated (non-system) workqueue which will send responses to it and unref the connection, an issue arises however in this application if the remote device disconnects prior to the task having finished, the application attempts to restart advertising using the system workqueue from the disconnection handler. The problem is that because the other task contains references to the connection, restarting advertising fails with error -12. Therefore the application is unable to restart advertising and then is in a dead state. Upping the connection count to 2 does work around this issue, but is not an acceptable solution due to the additional RAM usage (which is essentially wasted).
Some operations can also take longer than others, e.g. a image erase command can take upwards of 5 seconds to process.

**To Reproduce**
mcumgr has this issue

**Expected behavior**
To be able to restart advertising, from the system workqueue, triggered in the disconnect handler

**Impact**
Showstopper

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - Commit SHA or Version used: This is apparent in an nRF connect SDK sample application (samples/matter/lock) using the softdevice, but should be reproducible with any application that uses bluetooth, I did not attempt seeing if this issue was present in the zephyr controller but would imagine it would be given that it is caused by the limit of connection references/handles being reached
